s702_PP_r2: Hello! Happy to help. We use a before a consonant sound (a pen) and an before a vowel sound (an apple). Try this one: Write a or an: She has ___ orange in her bag. (answer with only the missing word)
s708_PP_r2: Hi! Good idea. Remember: a goes before a consonant sound (a book) and an goes before a vowel sound (an egg). Your first exercise. Write a or an: My uncle is ___ doctor. (answer with only the missing word)
s714_PP_r2: Hello! We use a/an the first time we talk about something, and the when we talk about it again. Example: I have a dog. The dog is brown. Now you try. Write a or the: We have a garden. ___ garden is small.
s720_PP_r2: Hello! We use can + the base verb to say what we are able to do. Example: I can swim. For no, we say can't: I can't sing. Now try this one. Correct the sentence: "She can swims."
s726_PP_r2: Hi! We use can + base verb (no -s, no to) for ability: I can swim. We use can't for things we are not able to do: I can't sing. Here is your first exercise. Correct the sentence: "She can swims."
s732_PP_r2: Hello! Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. The word I is always a capital letter. Example: My aunt lives in a big house. Now you try. Rewrite correctly: "my brother likes tea"
s738_PP_r2: Hello! In English we always need am, is or are in a sentence. We say I am, he/she/it is, and you/we/they are. Example: He is tired. Try this one. Write am, is or are: I ___ a student. (answer with only the missing word)
s744_PP_r2: Hi! Remember: I goes with am, he/she/it goes with is, and you/we/they go with are. In English we do not leave these words out. Here is your first exercise. Write am, is or are: She ___ at home today. (answer with only the missing word)
s750_PP_r2: Hello! We use at with clock times (at 7 o'clock), on with days (on Monday) and in with months (in July). Now you try. Write in, on or at: My train leaves ___ 5 o'clock.
s756_PP_r2: Hello! We use There is with one thing (There is a table) and There are with more than one (There are two chairs). Now you try. Complete: "___ three windows in my room."
s762_PP_r2: Hi! Use There is for one thing (There is a table) and There are for plural things (There are two chairs). Here is your first exercise. Complete: "___ three windows in my room."
s768_PP_r2: Hello! An English statement usually goes subject, then verb, then object. Place or time goes at the end. Example: Sam plays football on Fridays. Now you try. Put in order: "plays / Sam / chess / on Mondays"
s774_PP_r2: Hello! Let us learn classroom words. Example: This is a pen. This is a chair. Now you try. Complete: "I sit on a ___."
s780_PP_r2: Hi! Here is a classroom exercise. We say: This is a pen. This is a chair. Now you try. Complete: "The teacher writes on the ___."
s786_PP_r2: Hello! For time words, we use on with days (on Monday), in with months (in July) and at with clock times (at 7 o'clock). Now you try. Write in, on or at: They get married ___ April.
s792_PP_r2: Hello! We introduce family like this: This is my sister. She is ten. Use He for a boy or man and She for a girl or woman. Now you try. Complete: "This is my brother. ___ is twelve."
s798_PP_r2: Hi! When we introduce family, we say: This is my father. He is a driver. We use He for males and She for females. Here is your first exercise. Complete: "This is my grandmother. ___ is very kind."
s804_PP_r2: Hello! Let us practise food and drink words. Example: I like rice. I like apples. Now guess the word. Write the word: you drink it, it is white. ___
s810_PP_r2: Hello! Each room has a name and a use. Example: I cook dinner in the kitchen. My bed is in the bedroom. Now you try. Complete: "I make toast in the ___."
s816_PP_r2: Hi! We do different things in different rooms. Example: We wash our hands in the bathroom. There is a tree in the garden. Now you try. Complete: "My bed is in the ___."

Hello! Here is a short dialogue. Read it and find the final time they agree.

A: Is the lesson at nine?
B: No, it is at ten. Let us meet at quarter to ten.
A: OK, quarter to ten is good.

What time do they meet?
s828_PP_r2: Hello! To ask politely, we say Can I have ... please? instead of a blunt command. Example: Can I have a glass of water, please? Now you try. Make this polite: "Give me a coffee."
s834_PP_r2: Hi! In a cafe, we ask nicely: Can I have a glass of water, please? or I would like a tea, please. Here is your task. You are thirsty in a cafe. Ask for a tea politely.
s840_PP_r2: Hello! To compare two things, we add -er to short adjectives (fast, faster than) and use more ... than with long adjectives (more expensive than). Now you try. Complete: "Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
s846_PP_r2: Hello! We join short sentences with and (adds), but (shows a difference) and because (gives a reason). Example: I like tea and I like milk. Now you try. Join with and: "I have a cat. I have a dog."
s852_PP_r2: Hi! Use and to add, but to show a difference, and because to give a reason. Example: She is happy because it is Friday. Here is your first exercise. Join with but: "The bus is cheap. It is slow."
s858_PP_r2: Hello! In the present simple, we add -s after he, she and it. Words like always, usually, sometimes and never go before the main verb. Example: My brother usually gets up at seven. Now you try. Correct the verb: "She go to bed at ten."
s864_PP_r2: Hello! We use am/is/are + going to + base verb for plans. Example: I'm going to visit my aunt tomorrow. Now you try. Correct: "I going to study tonight."
s870_PP_r2: Hi! For plans, we say I am going to + verb. Do not forget am, is or are before going to. Example: She is going to visit her aunt. Here is your exercise. Complete: "They ___ (play) football next Saturday." (a plan)
s876_PP_r2: Hello! We use many with things we can count (many eggs) and much with things we cannot count (much rice). Now you try. Write much or many: How ___ bottles are there?
s882_PP_r2: Hello! For past questions we use did + subject + base verb. Example: What did you do last weekend? Answer: I went to the beach. Now you try. Make a question with did: you / go / to the park / on Saturday?
s888_PP_r2: Hi! To ask about finished actions we use Did + subject + base verb, with no -ed on the verb. Example: Did you go to the beach? Here is your exercise. Write a question with did: she / visit / her aunt / last weekend?
s894_PP_r2: Hello! Some verbs are irregular in the past, so we must learn them. Example: go becomes went, buy becomes bought. Now you try. Write the past form of 'have': Yesterday I ___ a big lunch.
s900_PP_r2: Hello! For finished actions we usually add -ed to the verb. Example: I walk becomes I walked. Now you try. Write the past simple of play: Last weekend I ___ football with my friends.
s906_PP_r2: Hi! In the past simple, regular verbs end in -ed (play becomes played, walk becomes walked). If the verb ends in e, add only -d (like becomes liked). Here is your exercise. Write the past simple of watch: Last night she ___ a film.
s912_PP_r2: Hello! We use am/is/are + verb-ing for things happening now. Example: Two children are playing football. Now you try. Imagine a park. Write two sentences about what people are doing now.
s918_PP_r2: Hello! We use some in positive sentences (I have some tea) and any in questions and negatives (Do you have any milk? I don't have any sugar). Now you try. Write some or any: Can I have ___ water, please?
s924_PP_r2: Hi! In a cafe we say: Can I have a coffee, please? We use some in positive sentences and any in questions and negatives. Here is your exercise. Write some or any: We don't have ___ sandwiches today.
s930_PP_r2: Hello! After he, she and it, we add -s or -es to the verb. Example: I work, she works. He teaches English. Now you try. Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
s936_PP_r2: Hello! We use has for he, she and it, and is or are to describe a person. Example: My aunt has long black hair. She is tall and cheerful. Now you try. Complete: "My cousin ___ brown eyes." (has / have)
s942_PP_r2: Hi! To describe someone, we can talk about their looks and their personality. Example: The doctor has blue eyes. He is calm. Here is your task. Write two sentences about a famous actor: one about hair or eyes and one about personality.
s948_PP_r2: Hello! To ask a price we say How much is this hat? for one thing and How much are the socks? for plural things. Now you try. Correct this question: "How much cost this hat?"
s954_PP_r2: Hello! Different jobs work in different places. Example: A teacher works at a school. Now you try. Complete: "A chef works in a ___."
s960_PP_r2: Hi! Let us match jobs to workplaces. Example: A teacher works at a school. Remember to use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound. Here is your exercise. Complete: "A pilot works at an ___."
s966_PP_r2: Hello! Let us practise weather words like sunny, rainy, cold, hot and windy. Example: It is sunny today. Now you try. Complete: "Take an umbrella. It is ___ today."
s984_PP_r2: Hello! Let us practise introducing family members. Use He for a man or boy and She for a woman or girl. Example: This is my father. He is a driver. Now you try. Complete: "This is my grandmother. ___ is very kind."
s990_PP_r2: Hello! After he, she and it, the verb takes -s or -es (works, teaches), and verbs ending in a consonant + y change to -ies (studies). Now you try. Write the correct form: The baby ___ (cry) at night. (answer with only the verb)
